content:
After translating coordinates, take \(A=(0,0), B=(p,q), C=(r,s)\), with \(\ell\) horizontal and \(m: x=a\).  
The circle centered at \((u,v)\) tangent to \(m\) has equation
\[
(x-u)^2+(y-v)^2=(u-a)^2.
\]

For \(A\) and \(B\), subtracting equations gives
\[
p(x-a)+q\left(y-\frac q2\right)=0.
\]
For \(A\) and \(C\),
\[
r(x-a)+s\left(y-\frac s2\right)=0.
\]
Let \(X=x-a\). Then
\[
pX+qy=\frac{q^2}{2},\qquad rX+sy=\frac{s^2}{2}.
\]
Since \(A,B,C\) are noncollinear, \(ps-qr\neq 0\), so
\[
X=\frac{qs(q-s)}{2(ps-qr)}.
\]
The condition that no two points lie on a line parallel to \(\ell\) gives \(q,s,q-s\neq 0\), so
\[
X\neq 0.
\]

The common point must be the radical center, so \(x=a+X\). Substituting into the circle centered at \(A\):
\[
(a+X)^2+y^2=a^2
\]
so
\[
2aX+X^2+y^2=0.
\]
Since \(X\neq 0\), this has exactly one real solution for \(a\). Therefore there is exactly one such line \(m\).

\[
\boxed{1}
\]
